#4348. 10 Legendary Shields You Should Have in Borderlands 4

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Legendary items are the prize you are searching for in Borderlands 4. They will help you complete your build, and carry you into the different levels of Mayhem Mode.

With over a year’s worth of content added to the game, there are plenty of legendary items, which means you need to start refining which ones are best for your characters. Once you have all your legendary weapons, including legendary assault rifles, you need to move on to legendary shields.

Shields will protect you, give you some additional buffs, and help you fight back against the swarms of psychos and Order Troops across Kairos. If you haven’t obtained them already, these shields are ones that you should definitely get.

One of the best shields from the base game of Borderlands 4 is the Super Soldier, as it literally enhances your abilities, turning you into someone who can run and shoot fast. It is almost like you took the super serum given to Captain America. There are plenty of references and easter eggs to find across Kairos, too.

The shield has the ability called Power Play, which gives you an overshield whenever the shield refills. This is great for procing abilities on weapons like the Ohm I got that get benefits from overshields.

Additionally, while your shield is full, it grants you 25% increased fire rate and 25% increased movement speed, which is amazing on characters like Rafa and Loveless who can amp up their movement speed. If you want to get this shield, you will need to farm Vile Lictor in Terminus Range.

There are some shields that will carry you far into the game, and then there are shields that are perfect starting shields that pack a punch, and are great for new characters. The Firewerks shield is perfect for any new character that you create.

This shield comes with the Bundled ability, which fires rockets at enemies each time you get a kill. These missiles deal fairly decent damage, making it easier to clear crowds of enemies quickly.

Of course, being a shield you want to get early, you would expect to be able to farm this weapon early in the game, which you can. You can get this shield from Spashzone in Riptide Grotto, which is near where you start the game. Some legendary farming locations are trickier to find than you may think.

A shield is meant to keep you safe from damage, and the Onion is all about that by offering you a means of negating damage for brief periods of time. Instead of a normal shield, this is an armor shield, meaning it has multiple segments.

The ability Shallot Shell makes it so you are immune to damage for a couple seconds after an armor segment breaks. Since this shield often has four segments, you have four times where you will be immune to damage before the shield is gone.

It is great for increasing your survivability, and is perfect for characters who are a bit squishy. You can obtain this shield by farming Sludgemaw at Watershed Gate.

How do Borderlands 4's new Vault Hunters stack up?

Do you want a shield that will cause some devastation each time it breaks and refills? Well, you might want to get your hands on the Extra Medium then, as it will cause some serious devastation.

This shield isn’t the most protective, with it sitting near the average when it comes to shield health. However, this is made up for by the ability Nucleosynthesis, which causes it to trigger a nova that deals major damage in the surrounding area each time it breaks or refills.

Of course, you need to let the shield completely refill before you can trigger the effect again, but it is great for getting out of sticky situations, and you can obtain this shield by farming the Vault Boss named Inceptus.

One of the biggest things that kills me in Borderlands 4 is self-damage. I blow myself up all the time with grenades and other types of splash damage. It is a serious issue. Luckily, the Honey Badger fixes this issue.

The Honey Badger shield has the Ferocity ability, which reduces self-damage dealt by 90%, meaning you can take a hit from a grenade and not get thrown into a fight for your life. It is the perfect shield for those who deal a lot of splash damage all around them with Torgue weapons.

Of course, if you don’t have this issue, you can skip over this shield, but it is worth it if you do. You can get the Honey Badger from Big Oil in the Bloodstained Hollow as part of the Vault of the Damned DLC. For more gear, check out the best DLC weapons.

There are some shields that have amazing abilities that boost your damage, but this damage buff comes at a cost. For the Protean Cell, this cost is the shield’s health. Luckily, it has a lot of health.

This shield has the Direct Current ability, which drains the shield over time, but grants you a bonus 40% shock damage. However, while this ability is active, you take direct damage, meaning the shield won’t protect you, so you need to be selective about when you use it.

Use this shield correctly, and you will rip through enemy health bars in seconds. Just don’t get carried away or it could mean the end of your character. You can get this shield from Fractis in Grindstone of the Worthy.

There are plenty of weapons in Borderlands 4 that have been added in DLC. Which ones of them are the best?

Every character can have some sort of status effect build, which makes the Exfoliatrix a great shield because it can be used efficiently by every character. You just need to be running a status effect build.

The ability of this shield is Exfoliatrix, which increases your status effect chance for six seconds each time an armor segment breaks. Additionally, whenever an enemy receives status effect damage, you recover a portion of the shield.

If you are constantly dealing status effect damage, you will be well protected by this shield, and you won’t need to worry about taking damage. You can get this shield by farming the Digi-Rifts on Providence Island in the FL4K and the Last Resort DLC.

An interesting ability that some shields have is that they can spawn kill drones that help you damage enemies. The Little Sister is one of these shields, and it does a great job taking down enemies.

It has the ability Sister, which grants you a kill drone whenever an armor segment breaks. This kill drone fights alongside you, mimicking the element of the gun you are using, and dealing 25% of the gun’s damage.

It is a perfect little partner to help you on the battlefield, and one that will continuously deal damage for you, helping you to wipe out groups of enemies. You can get this shield from Throne’s Experiments in Research Center B-0451. It can also be dropped from the chests at the end of the Takedown at the Hadron Abyss.

The Watts 4 Dinner shield is pretty similar to the Protean Cell shield, as they both grant you bonus shock damage. While the damage buff is less for this shield, it is a far better shield overall.

The Watts 4 Dinner shield has the ability Overshield Eater, which makes it so enemies have an 8% chance to drop an overshield when hit. Whenever you have an overshield active, you get a bonus 25% shock damage.

This is very easy to obtain, especially if you have skills on your character that grant overshield. Giving you a consistent 25% damage bonus is amazing, making this shield one of the best in the game. You can get this shield by farming Origo in the Vault of Origo.

Nova shields can be really strong, especially when they give you a damage buff and also release a nova. The Cindershelly is great because it does both of these things, making it easy to take down enemies.

This shield has the Glass ability, which makes it so you get a stack of resolve whenever the shield is damaged. Each stack of resolve grants you 2% damage reduction, and when full of stacks, this means you have a 50% damage reduction.

To top it off, when this shield breaks, it releases a nova that deals a set amount of damage, but this damage is increased by 25% for each stack of resolve you have, meaning you can do an insane amount of damage with the blast. You can get this shield from The Backhive in Dissected Plateau.

There are plenty of legendary assault rifles in Borderlands 4, and we will show you how to get them all.

#4345. Experts say high blood pressure guidelines are missing half the equation

For decades, one of the most common recommendations for lowering high blood pressure has been simple: eat less salt. But a new scientific report suggests that this advice may be missing an equally important part of the equation.

Researchers say that increasing potassium intake, rather than focusing only on reducing sodium, could lead to better blood pressure control. By addressing both nutrients together, this approach could strengthen efforts to prevent hypertension and reduce the risk of serious cardiovascular problems.

The potential impact is enormous. High blood pressure, also known as hypertension, affects more than 1.28 billion adults worldwide and is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease, including heart attacks and strokes. Although public health recommendations have traditionally emphasized cutting sodium, researchers now argue that getting enough potassium deserves just as much attention.

Sodium and potassium are essential minerals that help regulate fluid balance, nerve signaling, and muscle function. Both also influence blood pressure, but they affect the body in different ways.

Eating too much sodium can cause the body to retain additional fluid, increasing the pressure inside blood vessels. Potassium helps counter some of sodium's effects by supporting the kidneys in removing excess sodium through urine. It also contributes to the normal functioning of blood vessel walls, which plays an important role in maintaining healthy blood pressure.

In a new report, physicians and health experts argue that dietary recommendations should address these two minerals together. Rather than treating sodium reduction as the primary solution, they propose combining it with greater potassium consumption to achieve stronger results.

"It is time to view dietary interventions holistically because food components interact and physiology is integrative across systems," said Naomi Fukagawa, M.D. Ph.D., professor of medicine emerita at the Robert Larner, M.D. College of Medicine at the University of Vermont and first author on the report. "Growing evidence shows that increasing dietary potassium as well as reducing sodium intake work together to better manage hypertension."

A Major Rethink of Blood Pressure Guidelines

The report, published in the peer-reviewed American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, was supported by the IAFNS Sodium in Food and Health Implications Committee.

The researchers examined the scientific evidence underlying current sodium and potassium recommendations, along with practical ways to reduce sodium consumption and increase potassium intake. They also explored the obstacles to implementing these changes and identified areas where additional research and updated public health policies could help improve outcomes.

One of the central concerns is that many people consume too much sodium while getting nowhere near enough potassium. Both dietary patterns can contribute to elevated blood pressure, making them important targets for prevention and treatment.

Despite widespread efforts to encourage people to limit salt, average sodium consumption continues to exceed recommended levels. Meanwhile, potassium intake remains "far below optimal levels in both developed and developing nations," according to the authors.

This imbalance suggests that focusing primarily on what people should eat less of may be overlooking an important opportunity to improve cardiovascular health by encouraging them to consume more of a beneficial nutrient.

Potassium is naturally present in many familiar foods, including fruits, vegetables, legumes, and dairy products. Bananas, potatoes, beans, leafy greens, and yogurt are examples of foods that can help increase potassium intake.

Another possibility is replacing some sodium chloride, the main ingredient in ordinary table salt, with potassium salts. These substitutes can help reduce sodium while simultaneously increasing potassium, potentially addressing both dietary goals at once.

However, creating these products presents challenges for food manufacturers. Adding too much potassium salt can produce an unpleasant metallic taste, limiting how much can be used without affecting flavor. Manufacturers must therefore find a balance that improves nutritional content while keeping foods appealing to consumers.

Increasing potassium is also not appropriate for everyone. People with kidney disease or those taking certain medications may have difficulty regulating potassium levels, so potassium supplements and potassium-based salt substitutes should be used with medical guidance when these concerns apply.

A New Strategy for Fighting High Blood Pressure

The researchers emphasize that reducing sodium remains essential. Their proposal is not to abandon existing advice, but to expand it by recognizing that potassium intake is another major factor in blood pressure regulation.

The authors conclude that "dietary sodium reduction is a foundational strategy for hypertension prevention and management. However, new evidence supports a broadening of the current approach that focuses solely on sodium reduction and provides equal emphasis on increasing potassium intake."

For the more than one billion people living with hypertension, this shift in thinking could have significant implications. Instead of concentrating almost exclusively on reducing salt, future dietary recommendations may increasingly emphasize the combined benefits of consuming less sodium and more potassium.

The underlying message is straightforward: better blood pressure control may depend not only on what people remove from their diets, but also on what they add.

#4343. EA Is Closing Down Legendary Studio BioWare Amid More Job Cuts

Electronic Arts plans to eliminate roughly 400 positions in an upcoming round of job cuts, per a new report from Bloomberg, and will also be closing the doors on its long-time role-playing game maker BioWare.

Per Bloomberg's Jason Schreier, these cuts represent about three percent of EA's total staff, and roughly 50 at BioWare. A letter sent to staff today from EA's COO David Tinson and Chief Studios Officer Cam Weber said that they've taken a "hard look at our business" and will cut projects, including the next Mass Effect.

"As we focus on these larger opportunities, we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect," the letter reads. "We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly."

Sports, shooters (like Apex Legends), and Star Wars (including the next Jedi title) will continue apace at Electronic Arts. The publisher also has a new Iron Man game in the works, and plans are in the works for more Battlefield, as well as a new collaboration between Respawn and DICE. The staff letter also suggests a planned Sims game will be put on ice in favor of another venture, and that while Skate development will continue, EA will downsize the team working on it.

EA was fully acquired earlier this year by a number of investor groups, including Silver Lake, Affinity Partners, and the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, taking the publicly traded company private. In its announcement at the time, EA chairman and CEO Andrew Wilson said, "We're entering this next chapter from a position of strength with partners who share our vision and ambition. Together, we'll invest boldly, accelerate innovation, and build the next generation of games and experiences for the hundreds of millions of players and fans who inspire us every day."

A statement from BioWare posted to social media shared the closure as well, highlighting the list of games it has brought to life: Baldur's Gate, Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Dragon Age, Mass Effect, and Anthem. The team's focus now, per the statement, is on supporting one another through this transition.

"What generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember," the statement reads. "These games became so much more because you played them, debated your choices, fell in love with the characters, and made these worlds your own. From all of us at BioWare, thank you for being the most meaningful part of our story."

BioWare has been known throughout its history for exactly that: an undoubtedly legendary run of role-playing games where choice, characters, and moments matter. From the early era of D&D-driven adventures to leading the pack in console RPG development with KOTOR, Mass Effect, and Dragon Age, few Western RPG studios boast the legacy BioWare had.

Still, BioWare often sailed on troubled waters. The underwhelming releases of Mass Effect: Andromeda and Anthem tarnished the studio's pristine image in the eyes of some fans. Dragon Age: The Veilguard, the studio's most recent—and final—game was generally better received by critics, but spent a decade in development turmoil. Internal strife over the making of these massive RPGs was the subject of frequent reporting. The term "BioWare magic," referring to how the studio's games would finally come together in the twilight hours of development, became a sticking point as the years went on.

There is no denying, though, how BioWare has played an active hand in molding the role-playing genre over the years. Even a recitation of past works doesn't feel accurate to the impact; the influence of Mass Effect and Dragon Age alone is something we still see ripples of today. Even as other studios have taken up the torch and put their own spin on companion-driven, choices-matter stories, there is still an innate sense of "BioWare" that's hard to remove from those interactions and moments.

Layoffs have become distressingly commonplace, as cuts to legendary teams are announced at a never-ending pace. But to break news writing decorum, I had always hoped, throughout years of working in this industry, that I wouldn't ever have to eulogize a studio like BioWare. A place that shaped my own dive into video games, and I'm sure did the same for many, many others. A roof under which developers worked long hours to craft stories we'd carry with us for years. I'm thankful for that, and hope those affected find somewhere new that's rewarding of their talents.

#4342. Scientists discover a surprising clue to autism's origins hidden in the placenta

Scientists are still working to understand why autism develops. Genetics are known to play a major role, but researchers have also found that conditions during pregnancy can influence the likelihood of autism spectrum disorder.

A new study from Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory (CSHL) has uncovered a surprising connection between inflammation during pregnancy, changes in the placenta, and the development of autism-like traits in male mice. The findings suggest that certain developmental disruptions may begin much earlier than previously recognized, potentially offering new clues about autism's origins.

"To truly understand autism spectrum disorder, we have to look beyond the brain," CSHL Associate Professor Lucas Cheadle says. "Our work suggests that maternal immune activation and changes within the placenta are a gateway to autism for some unique individuals."

Scientists Identify an Early Window of Vulnerability

To investigate how inflammation affects fetal development, Cheadle and his colleagues triggered an immune response in pregnant mice at different stages of pregnancy. They used a substance that mimics the immune system's reaction to a viral infection without actually introducing a virus.

The researchers discovered that mouse fetuses were especially vulnerable when inflammation occurred 12.5 days into pregnancy. According to Irene Sanchez Martin, a postdoctoral researcher in Cheadle's laboratory, approximately one-third of the fetuses showed developmental abnormalities within just 24 hours.

Scientists have investigated the effects of maternal immune activation for decades, but these findings reveal signs of developmental disruption earlier than researchers had previously observed.

Even more striking was the difference between male and female fetuses. Across every experiment, autism-like traits appeared only in males, while females continued developing normally.

This unexpected distinction could provide insight into why autism is diagnosed substantially more often in boys than girls. What makes the finding especially intriguing is how early the difference appeared, before many of the biological changes normally associated with sex-specific development.

"It's really fascinating, because we're looking at an age which precedes hormonal surges. It precedes sexual differentiation in the brain and many other regions. So, it's surprising there would be a sex-based difference this early."

A Surprising Connection Between the Placenta and Autism

To determine why some developing mice were affected while others appeared protected, Cheadle and Sanchez Martin examined the placenta, the organ that connects a developing fetus to its mother and supports its growth throughout pregnancy.

Their attention centered on specialized cells called spongiotrophoblasts, which occupy a region of the mouse placenta where maternal and fetal cells interact.

In fetuses that developed normally, this part of the placenta remained healthy. However, male fetuses showing developmental abnormalities also had visible damage to these specialized cells.

Spongiotrophoblasts play an important role in helping the mother's immune system tolerate the developing fetus. This protection is essential because the fetus carries genetic material from both parents and is not genetically identical to the mother.

The researchers found that maternal immune activation could interfere with this protective function. When these placental cells become damaged, the mother's immune response may begin affecting the developing fetus in harmful ways.

Why Female Fetuses May Have a Hidden Advantage

The findings raise another intriguing question: Why were male fetuses vulnerable while females appeared unaffected?

One possibility is that male embryos produce distinctive proteins that can trigger an unfavorable maternal immune response following a viral infection. Another explanation is that female embryos possess some form of protection that helps them withstand inflammation during this sensitive developmental period.

Cheadle says, "A protective mechanism may exist within the female that could be harnessed to help the male. We're trying to understand how autism emerges in both sexes," he explains. "The evidence says that there are potentially different mechanisms."

These possibilities suggest that biological pathways involved in autism-like development may differ between males and females. Understanding those differences could help researchers identify why some individuals are more vulnerable to certain environmental influences during pregnancy.

Cheadle's team plans to investigate both male and female mice more closely to uncover the mechanisms responsible for these contrasting responses. Their work could eventually identify new targets for treatments and lead to strategies for intervening earlier in developmental processes associated with autism.

Although the findings come from experiments in mice and do not establish that the same mechanisms cause autism in humans, they highlight an unexpected possibility: Important clues to autism's earliest development may lie not only in the brain, but also in the placenta and its interactions with the maternal immune system.

#4341. Tomorrow’s Battlefield 6 patch is the first step towards improving footstep audio, and it might actually fix the settings reset bug

The next major Battlefield 6 patch is nearly upon us, and Battlefield Studios is promising a bounty of changes - including a couple of fixes to some big bugs.

Battlefield 6 is about to receive a new update. Version 1.1.3.0 is set to arrive tomorrow, December 9 to kick off the third and final phase of the game’s first season. Winter Offensive brings some holiday-themed new content to the game, but it’s not the most interesting part of the patch.

That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the new patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.

Thew new content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly. To go along with that there are new limited-time modes for both multiplayer and Redsec’s Gauntlet. The event mode will be available in Conquest, and Domination.

The Ice Climbing Axe is the only new weapon in this drop. The battle pass gets a new Winter Offensive bonus path, just like we’ve seen with previous seasonal stages. This is how you unlock the axe, too.

Easily the most interesting change in this update is the range of improvements to audio across the board. First, footstep audio received a big pass that should make it easier to hear enemy footsteps, easier to locate them, and across different surfaces.

Some of the bugs that caused certain sounds to simply vanish have been fixed. This was especially prevalent in battle royale matches. BF Studios explained in the patch notes that it has adjusted memory priorities for in-game sounds in order to prioritise the most crucial ones. This is not the end of the road on audio, however, as the developer continues to work on making the soundscape more stable and reliable.

Some of those audio changes are the result of recent testing done in Battlefield Labs, which is also responsible for another exciting addition in this latest patch: improvements to hit registration.

While BF6 has had solid and stable netcode, certain situations would sometimes create uncertainty about how you died, and why certain actions seemingly failed to perform at that particular moment.

The focus in this update is to improve the reliability of how actions in close-quarter combat are translated, which includes firing before fully going into ADS, quick aim changes and more.

Speaking of close-range, the patch also brings another pass to soldier visibility to make it easier for enemies to stand out from the background. This is particularly relevant in areas with low contrast, or busy environments with lots of particle and visual effects.

1.1.3.0 also brings yet another set of weapon handling and gunplay tweaks, this time focusing on accuracy issues with first shots. You can also expect more tweaks to attachment behaviour with regards to recoil.

Something else worth highlighting is that vehicle gameplay is getting several smaller tweaks that have to do with how they interact with the world, how their HUDs behave and more. Finally, your settings should no longer be reset after applying an update. BF Studios says there are still some instances where that might happen, but the issue should be fixed for the majority of players.

You can read the full change log on the Battlefield blog.
