#4311. Disney Speedstorm - Racers tier list

Updated on November 4th, 2026 - Version: 1.20.1 - Latest Additions: Miguel Rivera, Hector Rivera, Ernesto de la Cruz

It’s pretty much a fact that Disney boasts one of the widest rosters of characters and famous franchises, enjoyed by kids and adults alike. From Sleeping Beauty to Mulan and more, there are very few places and times that the Disney vault hasn’t touched upon. So it’s no surprise that they’re making their way to mobile again…although this time in a very different, high-octane way.

Disney Speedstorm is a kart racer that features characters from across the Disney world, split into four current (and growing) factions or teams of racers. These include: Beauty and the Beast, which features characters from the film; Hercules, Mulan, Mickey & Friends, Pirates of the Caribbean, The Jungle Book, Monsters Inc., Toy Story, Walt Disney World, Lilo & Stitch, and Aladdin.

Yes, it’s quite a stacked roster, and while many (if not all) of these films are aimed towards a younger audience, we know that more than a few readers probably have a hard time letting go of their enjoyment of the Disney classics, modern and otherwise. So we’re expecting quite a large, more skill-oriented and older audience that will have all the same questions that players of other, more hardcore games may ask.

For example, what differences do the racers have between each other, and which are the best to use? Well, for differences, quite a lot actually, as it wouldn’t be a character-based roster if you didn’t have variables between them. So, in the spirit of our previous coverage of many other games, we’ve brought together a brief tier list ranking all the characters in Disney Speedstorm, from the beauties to the beasts and deciding just where they fall on a firm ranking. Right out of the (Disney) vault Racers have different stats, including Top Speed, Acceleration, Handling, Boost and Combat. However, for the sake of argument, we’re going to take into account their subjective performance and aggregate against where they’ve placed elsewhere. It’s also worth noting that many players who prefer to play competitively have reportedly pursued a playstyle wherein they eschew upgrades or pit members (which are selectable upgrades that boost performance), so there’s a lot of debate about whether or not character difference matters for more casual play.

So, with our Disney Speedstorm tier list, you can get to grips with the huge variety of iconic characters taking to the racing circuit.

Without further ado, let’s get into it, starting with…

Characters in this tier are, obviously, top of the leaderboard when it comes to performance. Although stats make a huge difference, we’ve aggregated their placement against the general opinion and what we’ve seen from playing ourselves. Elizabeth Swann, for example, takes this spot for her consistent placement in the top tier; however, we have seen her drop in some estimations as more characters are added, with those like Buzz Lightyear shooting to the top consistently since his release.

It’s no surprise that Gaston places so consistently high. As the lyric goes, “No-one fights like Gaston”, and his skill, Trophy Hunting, essentially means he can use his special ability to knock out opponents consistently. And if you’ve got good aim, you won’t need to worry about how long it takes to refresh.

He also provides a pretty good example of what this tier is about. These characters possess exciting and varied skills and abilities that mark them out from the rest of the pack. However, for whatever reason, they still don’t rank highly in the reception of players. This could be simply because they don’t work out competitively, or that their abilities are done better by other characters in their faction.

It’s ironic that Disney’s poster boy is in this tier; however, it suits the fact that Mickey is somewhat of a difficult starting character. Especially due to his low top speed, which means that he can end up lagging behind other racers. However, we still place him fairly high because - well - he’s Mickey Mouse, and because the fact you’ll probably end up playing through the single-player missions starring him and soon upgrading this racer means that you won’t have to cope with his lacklustre starting stats for too long.

However, Mickey does have one crippling weakness, which is the fact his special ability - Trailblazer - not only boosts you…but also all the other racers behind you! It’s quite charitable, but not exactly the best if you’re hoping to leave other racers in the dust.

Getting down to the C tier, we have racers that are simply lacking in most departments. As we stated at the start, it’s difficult to nail down truly bad characters in any racer, as your skill is a crucial part of the performance. However, some of these characters possess abilities or drawbacks that are simply too prominent to ignore.

Hercules, for example, suffers one decisive drawback in his character, which is that his special ability not only actively aids his opponents, like Mickey’s does, but also makes them invulnerable! The only saving grace here is, of course, that this only applies to racers who follow the trail left by his ability, which means those up ahead won’t benefit. But it is a significant drawback, regardless.

Fortunately for the characters relegated to the bottom of this Disney Speedstorm tier list, there are no truly bad characters, as any of them can be relatively decent under the right circumstances. However, these characters lack the potential and high performance that marks out those in the upper tiers. Don’t fret if your personal favourite is in this tier, as you can still play them with reasonable expectations to take home some victories. Just don’t expect to breeze your way to victory, and be ready to work for your wins. As of the first version of this list, there’s fortunately only one character who’s had a cold reception across the board.

If you don’t know who Figment is, we don’t blame you, as he’s quite a deep cut even for Disney superfans. He’s actually the mascot for the Epcot attraction in Walt Disney World. Certainly, he’s not as popular as the other characters on this list and has had quite a muted reaction both competitively and casually. And it’s no surprise given his poor stats are balanced out only by a somewhat useful special ability in Spark of Imagination that can obscure other racer’s vision, but requires you to be in close proximity to a large number of them to get maximum utility - and only a short speed boost to compensate for the poor placement you’d need to either intentionally or accidentally be in to use it.

As always, we have the fans over at the Disney Speedstorm wiki to thank for having the information on each individual racer’s abilities and stats readily accessible. Their list has been invaluable and provides an easy way to compare racers out of the game, as well as some info on the trivia and easter eggs you can find on the characters’ racing suits and elsewhere. Thanks in part to a surprisingly robust character roster and equally exciting scenery and references to popular Disney films, there’s also a vibrant and thriving fan community to engage with when it comes to Disney Speedstorm.

Since you've lasted this long, we also have a Defense Derby tier list, as you're an avid fan of cars, obviously.

#4310. NAVI knock world No.1 Spirit out of PGL Masters Bucharest to set up Vitality quarter-final

Team Spirit are out of PGL Masters Bucharest 2026 before the playoffs. Natus Vincere, who knocked them out, now face a Vitality side using stand-in jL.

Team Spirit came into the deciding match as the HLTV.org world number one. The last 2-2 decider of the Swiss stage, against Natus Vincere, ended their event.

The match swung sharply. NAVI dominated the opening map on Cache. Spirit pulled level on Dust2, but it was NAVI who closed the series out on Anubis. HLTV reported that it was Spirit’s first defeat by NAVI since February 2025.

NAVI’s run to the playoffs was uneven. They opened with 2-0 wins over G2 and FURIA, and the second map against G2 went to three overtimes. Then the form dipped.

BetBoom beat them 2-0, on Dust II 10-13 and Nuke 9-13. Vitality followed, with NAVI losing Inferno 2-13 and Dust II 9-13. That second straight defeat dropped NAVI into the 2-2 pool, where one more loss would have ended their event.

Spirit took a similar route to the decider. They lost 1-2 to MOUZ on 27 October. Spirit won Nuke 13-2 but then lost Dust2 8-13 and Mirage 14-16.

Elimination at 2-3 has a clear financial cost. Teams finishing ninth to eleventh each receive US$31,250. Each losing quarter-finalist takes US$50,000. The winners’ share is split equally between players and organisation.

NAVI were not the only late qualifiers. Nemiga beat The MongolZ 2-0 and FURIA beat Liquid 2-0 on the final group-stage day. Those three teams took the last three playoff places.

The rematch comes quickly, against the Vitality side that beat NAVI in the group stage. The other ties are Nemiga v FUT, Aurora v MOUZ and BetBoom v FURIA.

Vitality are not at full strength. The organisation announced in August that Justinas ‘jL’ Lekavicius would stand in at BLAST Open Porto and PGL Masters Bucharest.

The stakes extend beyond this event. NAVI’s tournament page calls Bucharest the penultimate major tournament before the PGL Major Singapore 2026. A deep run here would give any of the eight teams momentum heading into that event.

#4309. Remedy Explains Control Resonant's Most Memorable, Unexpected Sequence And Its [REDACTED] Inspirations

Please allow the first sentence here to warn you that this interview discusses a portion of Control Resonant that takes place near the end of the game and is arguably the most unexpected and surprising sequence. I encourage you to experience it without spoilers. So if you haven't beaten the game yet, please do, and then come back to this page.However, if you have beaten the game, or curiosity has driven you to learn what game has been redacted from the headline and why (it's the 1995 Super Nintendo RPG, EarthBound, by the way), then please read on.

In the late-game of Control Resonant – basically right before you tackle the final confrontation – the game suddenly shifts timeframe and genre to become a 16-bit RPG. The nostalgic lens turns the game into something that feels like 1995's EarthBound, complete with turn-based battles, in order to explain the trauma that Jesse and Dylan went through at a young age after they came across an object of power: the slide projector. The whole sequence is funny, heartbreaking, weird, and importantly effective at making you feel you are seeing a part of their past. It was particularly effective on me as I have fond memories of playing EarthBound and games like it when I was young. To see and experience Dylan and Jesse's childhood this way felt accurate, as absurd as that sounds.

I reached out to Remedy to specifically discuss that portion of the game. You can find the full e-mail interview below with the team members who contributed to its creation.

The big RPG backstory sequence for Jesse and Dylan – why approach the storytelling that way?

Lead level designer, Anne-Marie Grönroos: The basis for the whole sequence is that the Hedron attacks Dylan's mind, breaks his reality apart, and he has to rebuild himself. We wanted the reality-breaking part to affect the game itself and have the player feel some of the confusion Dylan is feeling by breaking the fourth wall.

Who pitched that sequence, how did they pitch it, and was it difficult to sell to the larger team?

Grönroos: At Remedy, ideas rarely come from a single person or team, and we rarely do formal pitches, but rather discuss and workshop ideas cross-craft until they start taking the shape of something we like. The initial idea from the writer was for this to be a text-based adventure, to return to a very early form of a video game to show that the Patterning is devolving him, but an Alan Wake 2 DLC had already done that, and we wanted to find something else.

Independently, some months ago a level designer had suggested a sidequest with JRPG pixel graphics, but that had gone nowhere. I remembered that and suggested doing an old Final Fantasy-style JRPG here, which also felt more fitting since that’s the type of game Dylan and Jesse would have played in their childhood, and not a text-based adventure. People got excited about that, and after some concerns about feasibility, we went forth with it. It helped that the level designer who had originally wanted to do the JRPG side quest is a big fan of these types of games and has made them before. I wouldn’t have dropped something this crazy on someone who wasn’t passionate about it and ready to figure out how to do it with our engine that’s not built for anything like this.

Is EarthBound (Mother in Japan) the primary inspiration for that sequence? Are there big fans of those games at Remedy?

Senior level designer in charge of the JRPG quest, Arhi Makkonen:The whole Quest was born from that childhood feeling I had when playing old JRPGs – Final Fantasy, Breath of Fire, Chrono Trigger, Secret of Mana, Bahamut Lagoon, and yes, Mother. The most important thing for me was capturing that feeling of a time when games felt like magic. I think many people can relate to that nostalgia, and now Jesse and Dylan share that feeling in the game.Visually, Mother was a major inspiration of course. Juuso Anttila is the concept artist who did all the splendid pixel art for Rebuild quest. Mother's style fits the mysterious Americana small town vibe perfectly. We also couldn't pass up the pun about a story revolving around "Not-Mother" that was made in the style of Mother.

Was it difficult to implement the sequence into the game? Did Remedy's Northlight Engine need significant work to account for the sequence?

Makkonen: The Northlight engine was designed to work perfectly for third-person action games. Well, Rebuild Quest is pretty much the opposite of that. Northlight is a specialized tool rather than a general-purpose one, so we had to come up with some rather creative solutions to create a 2D JRPG.

First of all, we’re faking the 2D look. In reality, the entire JRPG Ordinary exists within a 3D world that the camera simply views from directly overhead. It occupies a tiny patch in a remote corner of the game world—a space where 3D Dylan would barely have room to stand. The entire game-within-a-game is written in Lua; our incredibly versatile game designer, Tommi Saalasti, created the underlying system, upon which I was then able to build the story.

Since we didn't really have the tools to create a game like this, I had to hand-code every single detail. Dylan takes one step up, Dylan turns left (where Jesse hopefully is at that moment), text box 1, text box 2. The Lua script for the Rebuild quest alone probably contains as many lines of code as all the other quests in the game combined. And then there were things like animations were restricted to a maximum of two frames, and some UI elements were created using static particle effects.

So yes, we faced all sorts of challenges and compromises, but at the heart of it all was a wonderful story – simply told in a somewhat unconventional way. We trusted that the narrative would make up for some of the imperfections.

Remedy has a reputation for big unexpected and often crazy singular moments. What are the conversations like around delivering those? In pre-production, are there conversations like, "What is the big moment for this one?" Or do they happen pretty naturally?

Grönroos: They both happen naturally and we also have conversations about what the big moments should be. Sometimes we like a section so much that we decide to put even more resources and importance to it, even if it wasn’t supposed to be all that important from the get-go. The Into the Sinkhole quest, for instance, is a quest that wasn’t planned to be a “tentpole moment” from the start, but we kept putting more effort into it when it was shaping up to be something very special.

But most setpieces in the game were planned to be such from the early stages of pre-production. In Resonant, we wanted to have multiple standout moments instead of a single sequence like the Ashtray Maze overshadowing everything else, and I’m happy to see that players have different favorites.

And a different approach from Control is that several of these memorable moments (Sinkhole, Underpass Fault, the JRPG section) are more emotional and subdued instead of bombastic action (although we also have big action setpieces), which was an interesting challenge itself.

Was there a fear that the visuals would limit the emotional impact of the sequence?

Grönroos: Yes, but we decided to trust the writing. Several other games have managed to deliver a similar emotional impact despite pixel graphics (and sometimes because of them, since the level [of] abstraction can make characters more relatable and up to the player’s interpretation), so we weren’t too concerned.

Was there a fear that action game fans would be frustrated by the RPG sequence?

Grönroos: Yes, this was the main concern about the sequence. It was a very polarizing sequence in the playtests: people either loved or hated it. We did discuss shortening it significantly, but in the end decided to keep it as it is but added some fast travel options and make some parts skippable. There were more fans than haters, and we didn’t want to sacrifice something we really enjoyed.

How concerned were you about the actual RPG mechanics of that sequence?

Makkonen: Since Rebuild doesn't feature a vast number of battles, we didn't need to build particularly deep RPG or progression systems. The combat served as an additional storytelling tool – illustrating how bullies torment Dylan, showing his first fight (against rats, naturally), and depicting his eventual abduction by the FBC.

Refining the combat to be simple, yet offer the player meaningful choices required a few iterations. In addition to standard attacks, the children can occasionally use special abilities: Dylan delivers a heavy blow to a single enemy, while Jesse fires at everyone. Enemies deal enough damage that defending becomes necessary when multiple foes target the same character.

The lightbulbs in The Underpass mission goes in similarly unexpected, animated directions. How did that mission come about? What was the pitch like for that one?

Grönroos: That one started with the idea of doing something comically mundane, switching lightbulbs, and adding a paranatural twist to it. The cartoon man wasn’t in the initial version, but instead we were going to do live action videos and have Dylan get stuck in that video as the end twist. They were supposed to be old-fashioned “work safety” videos explaining how to change lightbulbs, and as the quest went on, it became more and more obvious that the maintenance guy in the videos was too aware of what Dylan was doing. This all came out from a one-hour workshop.

There wasn’t really a pitch, but rather a back-and-forth like “could we do a quest about Dylan changing lightbulbs in a ritualistic way? We could have these sentient work safety videos explain how to do it and “Dylan could get trapped inside the video.” Much later, when the live action turned out to be a no-go, we pivoted to the current cartoon instead, and that was even funnier than our initial idea.

Zenless Zone Zero' is saying goodbye to 2025 with a bang, as update 2.5 gets fully revealed.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered the good news on Version 2.5, To Be Fuel for the Night. This chapter is a big deal for a few reasons, not least of which because it brings an end to Season 2.

To start with, Version 2.5 arrives on December 30, making it the game’s last major update of the year, which also means players are in for some freebies to celebrate the new year.

Of course, the biggest addition in Version 2.5 is Ye Shunguang, the game’s new Agent, who’s a Void Hunter, and also Zenless Zone Zero’s first dual-form Agent. Zhao also becomes a playable Agent as part of this update - two things HoYoverse teased last week at The Game Awards.

Ye Shunguang’s unique attribute is Honed Edge, through which she can enter an Enlightened Mind state. Ye Shunguang’s signature Ether Veil can deliver Honed Edge damage as she applies a vulnerability effect to enemies. She arrives alongside her sidekick, Bangboo Sprout, who keeps with her swordplay theme by calling down flying swords.

Zhao is the other playable Agent as mentioned, an S-Rank Ice Defence legend. Zhao is a fast and nimble attacker who uses her giant greataxe to suppress enemies. Zhao can trigger Ether Veil: Wellspring by using Frostbite she accumulates, which buffs the entire squad.

Narratively, this particular chapter will reveal the fate of Waifei Peninsula. The quest is gonna take the squad deeper into the Lumite Mine ruins, and the new Perception Technique is how you’ll uncover the answers hidden within.

There’s a gameplay component to that, too. Ye Shunguang's Bladeflash Mirage ability will come in handy during the story’s big investigation, which comes with unique rewards, including a new W-Engine.

Version 2.5 is also the one set to give players the first taste of multiplayer combat thought he limited-time Joint Investigation: The Divine Maze event. As part of that, you can have three-Agent squads face off against each other in unique combat challenges.

There’s even more to get excited about in this one. Proxy Outpost lets you create your own Outposts, and join those created by other. This is more of a social feature than anything, though.

HoYoverse is also making a series of updates to Soldier 11, Grace, Soldier 0 – Anby, Ellen, and Burnice, all of whom will see their mechanics updated and their effectiveness boosted. Similar updates are on the way for other Agents, which will arrive in future updates. Shiyu Defense and Deadly Assault has seen some adjustments to the gameplay loop, too.

Finally, HoYoverse is making it easier for players to jump into 2.5’s new story chapter using Advance Screening. Ye Shunguang and Zhao will be available for the entire update’s duration, and reruns in the second half will guarantee another S-Rank.

You’ll be able to pick from Alice, Soldier 0 – Anby, or Astra. Zhao will herself be available as a login bonus alongside 1,000 Polychromes, a new outfit for Jane, and more. If you’re looking to jump in on December 30, don’t do so without having a look at our Zenless Zone Zero codes page to get some freebies.

She will help you to get through dungeons like Deesa or the Ancient Altar very quickly. Notes on Serena Serena the Battle Angel is an S-tier list support hero. One of her strengths is single-target healing for her teammates. She is a very useful hero who will be able to keep her ally tanks alive without issue. The only small inconvenient thing about this hero is that she does not have enough AoE healing to heal an entire team.

The characters in A-tier are also very good, almost as good as the characters in the S-tier list. The reason they did not get into the list above is that the A-tier characters have minor flaws that prevent them from being even better.

Notes on Randall Randall is considered an excellent DPS character, smashing everyone and everything in his path. Despite his assassin class, many people make Randall a tank by giving him HP and armour. The reason why you should pick this hero, though, is that he buffs his and his team's attack. Similar content:

Notes on Rakkana A strong character who does good damage to enemies. At the start of the battle, he attacks the opponent's back lines and lands a few well-aimed strikes, destroying most of the back line. After creating havoc, it's much easier to get complete control of the battlefield.

The characters in the B tier are average in terms of their power. They are not bad, but they are not exactly top-notch either. These heroes are great as support or as extra force, but not as the main units on the battlefield.

Notes on Artas Artas is a pretty good character who can kill enemies of average difficulty. It is worth remembering his abilities. Artas chooses one enemy within his range and deals damage equal to 640% of his defense, putting the enemy in vengeance state for nine seconds. Enemies in this state will become main targets for Artas and have their damage decreased by 8% and each 5% HP lost will further decrease the damage of the enemy by 1% for up to 15%. Notes on Hyupnos Hyupnos is a good character who will be a great support on the battlefield. His power surge casts Arcane to suppress an enemy. The suppressed enemy cannot use any actions for three seconds, making them almost useless. During the process, it will continue to deal significant damage to the enemy, which is convenient.

This tier includes characters you should not waste your resources and time on, as they don't bring much to the battlefield. Instead, they will just take up a slot that a much more useful character could occupy.

Notes on Omar He could be described as a pretty good hero who would definitely help you in the early stages of the game. However, he is not likely to help you when you are already at the end game.

We hope that we have highlighted a lot of useful information for you and helped you choose a hero you like and that will bring you victory. Be sure to visit us again, because the tier list will be updated all the time as soon as new updates and heroes appear in the game. #4306. 10 Pokémon Battles That Break the Rules of the Games

Laurence Wall is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been writing professionally since 2022 and covering games since 2023. He primarily writes guides and lists, with a focus on indie games, RPGs, ARPGs, Soulslikes, MMOs, card games, boss fights, and detailed tutorials. Before joining DualShockers, Laurence worked as

Pokémon games have never really been much of a challenge. I mean, that’s why Nuzlockes are so popular, right? You need to artificially inject some difficulty into the titles to really make the formula work.

However, while most trainers and Pokémon in the series follow the rules, others sometimes break them in one way or another. Intentionally or otherwise, this creates some of the more interesting challenges as the devs try to balance scales that are invariably tipped in our favour.

Let’s look at some of the most interesting examples, and why they make for such fascinating encounters.

This one is pretty famous, especially if you’ve ever Nuzlocked Ultra Sun and Moon! But why does this battle break the rules?

For starters, this battle is more like a trainer battle: you can’t run from this fight or catch Necrozma. No, it must be defeated! And if that wasn’t annoying enough, as soon as you enter the fight, Necrozma gains +1 to every stat.

On top of that, Necrozma has great coverage with its moveset and the ability Neuroforce, making its super-effective attacks even more potent. The thing is, you might have seen inherent stat boosts before, but they were from Totem battles! Necrozma isn’t even a totem Pokémon, and still gets a ridiculous amount of buffs. Getting through this battle without losing a single Pokémon is a massive challenge.

This list covers some of the best Pokémon ROM hacks to attempt a nuzlocke challenge.

I remember the first time I played Pokémon Yellow and ran into the Ghost. Honestly, the whole vibe of Lavender Town and the Pokémon Tower really freaked me out. But then again, I think I was like 4 or 5! Now this Ghost isn’t a Gastly; it isn’t even a Pokémon… not until you have the Silph Scope at least!

Of course, we all know it’s a grieving Marowak, but oddly enough, even though this really should be a regular Pokémon battle, you can’t catch this Marowak, no matter how hard you try. At least Necrozma gets an excuse; Marowak isn’t even legendary.

The thing is, though, in the original Generation 1 games, you can use a Poke Doll to escape the battle. If you do it this way, the battle is considered over, and you're the victor.

The Pokémon Mystery Dungeon series is pretty infamous for having ridiculously unfair battles that pit you and your partner against a massive number of opponents. Whether it's the entire cast of your Guild or Darkrai and 6 other Pokémon from the Dungeon surrounding you! But you always come out on top!

Well, one of the most annoying things that always seems to happen in these games is that your victory often means very little. For example, in the Grovyle fight at Crystal Lake, it doesn’t matter whether you win or lose; the story plays out as if you lost.

The same is true of the battle against Snover in Bidoof’s Special Episode. Even if you find a way to win, the game assumes you lost, so putting in extra effort and using items in these fights is pretty pointless.

Generation 5 is pretty famous for having Pokémon with stupidly high evolution levels. Whether it’s Mienfoo at level 50, Pawniard at level 52 or Larvesta at level 59. Of course, the most famous of these is Zweilous, the Pseudo-Legendary of the games, which evolves into Hydreigon at an eye-watering level 64.

The thing is, if you remember playing the original Black and White and facing off against Ghetsis at the end, you’ll remember he has a Hydreigon as his ace. And, for some magical reason, it's level 54. On the one hand, I get Game Freak wanting to give cool, powerful Pokémon to trainers and give us a challenge, but 10 whole levels under? Whatever happened to treating your Pokémon with love and respect?

Ah, and speaking of having underleveled Pokémon, we have another cheater in our midst. The thing is, Lance actually commits another assortment of sins alongside having illegal Pokémon.

Let’s ignore his 3 underleveled Dragonite for now, and take a look at his Generation 1 and 2 movesets. First, as part of the Elite 4, Lance has a Dragonite with Barrier, a move it cannot learn in that generation. He shoots himself in the foot a little with this, however, as the battle AI is coded to always use super-effective moves, even if they don’t actually do any damage. So he will always use Barrier against, let’s say, a Gengar, because of its poison typing.

And he commits another error in the next Johto titles, where he has an Aerodactyl with Rock Slide, another move that can’t be learned in Generation 2. Either Lance is a huge cheater, or maybe he just knows some secrets that we don't!

This list covers the hardest Elite Four members from Generations 1-9 of the Pokémon games.

While Generation 8 certainly wasn’t my favourite, it did have some odd yet memorable moments. One of these shows up when you fight Opal, the Fairy-type gym leader of Ballonlea.

This battle introduces some fairly bizarre mechanics, not found anywhere else in the series. As the battle goes on, Opal will ask you questions about herself. If you get them right, then great, you’ll get a nice little stat boost. But if you get them wrong, your Pokémon's stats will actually decrease. Yep, not from a move or an item, but a piece of trivia, mid-fight.

And the thing is, the last of these isn’t even true. You have to lie to Opal, saying she looks younger than she actually is, to get the final stat boost! Of course, this fight wasn’t actually difficult, but it’s still an odd event!

And speaking of Generation 8, we have another major cheater over here. You’ll meet Avery in your adventure through the Isle of Armour DLC for Pokémon Shield.

Avery considers himself a bit of a rival, and as such, he will do anything to win. In the 3rd trial, you’ll battle Avery again; however, in this match, he will set up Psychic Terrain before the fight even begins!

Psychic Terrain is a pretty strong move that boosts the power of all Psychic moves by 50%, and it usually takes a full turn to set up. Unless, of course, Avery had a Tapu Lele… which he doesn’t! He realises this is wrong afterwards and pays the price! Good riddance, eh?

If you have Pokémon Sword, instead of facing off against Avery, you’ll meet Klara, who fills a similar role, acting as your rival as you progress through the DLC.

Like the previous encounter, during the 3rd Trial, Klara will scatter a load of Toxic Spikes on the field before the battle even begins, which feels a bit more devious. And this isn’t just 1 layer of spikes, but 2, meaning that you’ll have the Toxic variant instead of the regular poison! Because Toxic Spikes doesn’t wear off like Psychic Terrain, you’ll need to Rapid Spin these away, or send out your own Poison-type to absorb the poison.

The funny thing about these cheaters is that I actually really like this added challenge in Pokémon games. Lately, the titles have become laughably easy, perhaps because we’re a little older. So having your opponents cheat and get extra turns certainly levels the playing field a little bit.

Pokémon Colosseum and XD are some of my favourite Pokémon games of all time. They brought so much personality to the Pokémon animations, and the world feels much more alive and dangerous than in other titles.

At the end of XD, you’ll face off against Greevil, and realise he actually gets 7 Pokémon instead of 6! First off, you’ll have to face the awesome Shadow Lugia, XD001. If you like, you can end this battle immediately with a Master Ball, but if you want to catch it with something more interesting, like a Premier Ball, it is a rough fight.

Once that’s done, Greevil will battle you directly with a full team of Shadow Pokémon. Oh, and did I mention Shadow Moves are super effective against every regular Pokémon type? And if all that wasn’t enough, he also has the 3 Legendary Birds! Yep, this guy's team is absolutely stacked! What a brilliant fight!

Of course, if you thought that 6v7 was brutal, Volo will totally rock your world. The first time I fought Volo, his team caught me totally off guard. I knew as soon as I saw the Spiritomb and heard that classic music track that this was going to feel like a fight against Cynthia.

Cynthia is famously one of the hardest battles in all of Pokémon, being the Champion of the Sinnoh region. Now imagine if she had a Giratina that emerged after she was defeated… and then you had to defeat that Giratina twice, once in its Altered Form, and once in its Origin Form, all without being able to revive or heal your team. Yep, this was a truly unfair 6v8 battle, and it was glorious.

This is what I meant earlier about trainers who cheat. They make for some of the coolest moments in the series. Why would the main villain let you walk all over them and still abide by the rules? They would try to defeat you by any means possible, right?

So having Volo with effectively 8 Pokémon, plus a Legendary, made for one of the craziest and coolest battles of all time. I’m not sure any other trainer will live up to the awesomeness of that final battle! We will have to wait and see!

#4305. FC 26 adds upgraded Pina alongside 3 new Heroes in full Winter Wildcards promo

Winter Wildcards Team 1 is scarier than Ultimate Scream, featuring buffed Pina, Dembele, Valverde and Rodman cards alongside brand-new Heroes.

EA Sports has revealed 3 new Heroes coming to FC 26 Ultimate Team as part of Team 1 of the Winter Wildcards promo: Ivan Zamorano, Claudio Pizarro and Jill Scott.

The Bayern and Werder Bremen legend Claudio Pizarro is famously the Bundesliga’s oldest ever player, after turning out well past 40 years of age - up front no less. But he’s making an appearance in FC 26 because he won the Hero Vote Poll a few months ago, with the Peruvian edging out notable nutter Steffan Effenberg and the prolific Brazilian striker, Elber.

The love for South American Heroes continues with Ivan Zamorano presented in his Real Madrid guise rather than part of the unbelievably stacked Inter squad which featured legends and Icons ranging from current Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone to Javier Zanetti and Ronaldo Nazario.

And probably most interestingly, Queen of the Jungle and centurion Lioness, Jill Scott, is also coming to shore up the midfield with a card which fits the “Gullit Gang” pre-requisite of all face stats over 80 - including a dominant 91 physical befitting her role as one of the most recognisable enforcers in women’s football.

Whether her in-game body type will actually let her put that strength out on the pitch (she will surely also have Bruiser) remains to be seen, but she could easily have the gangly aura of Patrick Vieira if the rest of her PlayStyles are right.

New Ultimate Team Heroes have been added mid-season before, including the likes of Enzo Francescoli in FC 24, but 3 at once looks to indicate that EA is leaning on Heroes to add fan-favourite players to the game with a lower threshold than Icons.

Plus they can be given away for free without upsetting the power curve as much as Icons, as shown by the free Classic XI Heroes handed out recently (I got Mario Gomez, F).

The rest of the Winter Wildcards team features a host of equally famous, and now infamous, players with some featuring 99 stats and alternative positions.

Highlights include striker and CAM versions of Balon D’or holder Ousmane Dembele, but also everyone’s love-to-hate Low Driven Shot master, Claudia Pina.

There are also incredibly strong-looking Gabriel and Fede Valverde cards, as well as downgraded, and therefore hopefully cheaper, versions of Icons like Johan Cruyff.

#4303. Adventure of White Chord tier list - Who's your favourite heroine?

Updated on November 4th, 2026 - Version: 1.6.3

We have ranked every single heroine on our Adventure of White Chord tier list, so you know exactly who you should equip as your main hero if your goal is to destroy all the enemy waves and progress through the story stages. Of course, you can also use the heroines in the dungeons, but the difficulty of those doesn't compare to the end-game battles in the story mode.  How to pick the best hero in Adventure of White Chord Selecting one hero to help you push through the stages is pretty simple early on. You won't have much choice, but to make things easier, you should redeem the latest Adventure of White Chord codes, since you'll get some free heroes from the codes too (Mephisto)!

If wondering how to assemble your team, it's pretty simple. You want to take into account the following:

All these play an important role, so if you want to pass the stages easily, these are the elements you need to pay attention to.

In the early game, it won't matter too much, so you can just equip your strongest (strongest gear, strongest pets, strongest skills), but the more you progress, the more they will make a difference.

Adventure of White Chord tier list breakdown The tier list we've created focuses on the end-game and which heroes perform the best. There are several options, and I recommend you go for the ones in the S tier or S+ tier. As a general rule of thumb, if you happen to get Wige & Weisse, you should always use them. They're the absolute best in Adventure of White Chord, at least for now.

Now then, let's take a look at the tier list! S+ tier  |  S tier  |  A tier  |  B tier  |  C tier Original article by Cristina Mesesan. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

Wige & Weisse are the best heroes, earning them the spot at the pedestal of our Adventure of White Chord tier list. It's two heroes in one, belonging to the Aurous rarity. They have a combination of Fire and Water attacks, which also boost Water and Fire damage. Once you get them, you should equip them, even at level 1.

Elise of Light is a physical damage dealer who focuses mainly on basic attacks, but also on increasing ATK Speed, Crits, and basic attack bonus. She is great if you want a hero who can generally be good for clearing content with any pet.

Odette is one of the best AoE damage dealers of Legendary rarity. She is ranked so high because her skill boosts the Skill DMG Bonus of herself and the pets, which is a huge deal. Since she buffs pets, she basically makes your entire team a lot stronger.

Niella could be one of the best DPS heroes in Adventure of White Chord if she's upgraded. She deals a lot of flat Water damage, and her kit revolves mainly around boosting her Skill and ATK Speed.

Nidhogg is decent because of her Physical trait, which is overall good. She doesn't have any elements, but she has increased Skill Damage Bonus, which scales really well into the late game.

Surtur is similar to Nidhogg, except that she belongs to the Fire element. She has insane Attack Speed, but also applies Burn Points to enemies, which deal additional damage.

Ankh deals Wind damage, and she can boost her Wind DMG Bonus. Her basic attacks deal additional Wind damage, and a lot more Wind damage if she deals a Crit. She also has pretty low Cooldowns once she is upgraded.

Yang Yuhuan relies on her Fire basic attacks to do the work. She can boost her Basic ATK DMG Bonus, but also her ATK Speed and Fire DMG Bonus. She deals more damage the lower her HP goes, which can be good in certain scenarios (mainly dungeons).

Cordelia is one of the very few heroes with a skill that is more defensive than offensive. She can gain a shield and regen some of her HP, which is also good situationally. She's not ideal for the story mode, but for some dungeons, she can be really useful.

Mahou Shoujo is a Mythic hero who can inflict Weathering Points on the enemy. She is available for free to new players, which is useful, especially in the early game. She is quite strong towards early-mid game, but not ideal for the later stages.

Odile and Pamina are two Epics, and the only Epics we have right now. Odile is Water-type, while Pamina is Physical, but both of them are pretty average (or rather, below average) when it comes to how good they are in end-game scenarios.

Odile is available for free for just logging in and doing your dailies for 7 days, so she is a good hero to use until you have something better (preferably from the S or S+ tier).

All the characters in the last section of our Adventure of White Chord tier list are okay in the early game until you get something better, but they tend to fall off ever so slightly towards the end-game. They are not that rare (they are mainly Mythic or Rare), which means their basic stats are a lot lower than some of the Legendaries'.

I recommend you only use them until you get something better, since you have no chances of getting Legendaries until you upgrade your gachas to higher levels.

In case you love ranking characters and comparing them as much as we do, we've got a Wittle Defender tier list, and in case you're a fan of MMOs, then take a peek at our Etheria Restart tier list too.

#4302. Heartopia finally gets a release date... on everything but Steam

Heartopia may very well be the first big game you play in 2026.

Heartopia developer XD Games has delivered the news anyone who tried out the life sim game had been waiting for. The Animal Crossing-like cozy multiplayer game will finally arrive on January 7 across Android, iOS, and PC - with one caveat.

The Steam version won’t actually launch on that date, and will instead go live at some other point in the future. You will be able to play it on PC through TapTap, which is the same emulator you may be familiar with from beta.

Pre-registration is open on the official website for all platforms. If you throw in your email address, you’ll receive a bundle of in-game items at launch. You’ll get 4,000 Gold, 20 Wishing Stars, 400 Moonlight Crystal, and 60 Exhibition Passes.

Interestingly, XD Games isn’t saying what you can expect from the launch build - in terms of content - just yet. Those details will be revealed closer to the January launch, so perhaps expect them in the first few days of the year.

If you created a character in either (or both) of the recent closed beta tests, you’ll also receive the Blueberry Crossbody Bag in-game cosmetic. If you made it to level 18 in either test, you’ll also get the Star Mascot Head cosmetic. Both items will be available to claim at launch.

We’ve spent a lot of time playing the game’s recent tests, and we’ve put together some early guides on how to get Roaming Oak Timber, how to unlock and upgrade hobbies and more. We also have a few cooking recipes to share with you.

#4301. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 23, 2026

This week has been home to some disheartening news. BioWare, the creators of games like Mass Effect and Dragon Age, is being shut down amid a flurry of layoffs. It's another frustrating story from a struggling video game industry. Below you will find some of our stories about the legendary developer, including our massive 2016 oral history. And then after that, you can read about our recommendations of what to play this weekend.

I spent the early hours playing Final Fantasy Resonance trying to figure out precisely why I couldn't put it down. I eventually realized that the game manages in a very purposeful way to answer that quiet need I've so frequently had: "I wish I could experience a game just like Final Fantasy IV or VI again, for the first time, but with a new cast and story." That's pretty much what you can expect here; Resonance is a very purposeful throwback experience that harkens to the early days of FF pixel adventures, but with several modern conveniences, graphical flourishes, and depth added into the mix. It's a big and refreshingly wholesome journey of entertaining party members, summoning giant creatures, flying an airship across the world, and fighting turn-based battles that include absurd spell effects. It's one of my favorite games of the year, and well worth the time it will take to explore. Read our full review for more.

Expect to hear a lot of people proclaiming this as "one of the good ones," as Modern Warfare came out swinging this week with a strong campaign, compelling additions to competitive multiplayer, and an impressive extraction shooter mode in the form of DMZ. I've already been impressed by the first few hours of the campaign, which offers a tense, harrowing, and often disturbingly brutal story that bounces between a number of character perspectives. The gunplay feels tuned in, the traversal and melee is satisfying, and the narrative beats grounded in excellent actin performances. Our reviewer has spent even more time with the full game, and can share their full perspective to help inform whether you want to take a dive into this year's installment.

The Nintendo Sports franchise, which began with Wii Sports in 2006, has never been about the single-player experience. That remains true 20 years later in Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. But this time around, Nintendo has boosted the amount of content beyond what the series has typically provided, appealing to all player counts, all while retaining its trademark approachability. Whether you're joining together with three friends for some friendly competition across the package's 12 sports or you're trying to climb the Island Crown ladder by beating increasingly difficult single-player opponents, Switch Sports Resort is a great motion-controlled collection.

Halloween is around the corner. As you’re buying overpriced candy, deciding which version of the Joker to dress up as, and debating between watching Obsession and Backrooms over a cup of cider, it’s the perfect time to replay old horror games or dive into new ones. 2026 has a solid roster of choices for the latter thanks to releases like Resident Evil Requiem, Paranormasight: The Mermaid’s Curse, and Silent Hill: Townfall, but Tenebris Somnia shouldn’t be overlooked if you’re looking for a cool indie throwback.

Part retro-inspired adventure game, part live-action indie horror film, you’ll uncover the mystery of a nightmare-induced apartment building and battle horrors to rescue your trapped ex. The gameplay is survival horror 101, but it’s executed well, with consistently clever and inventive puzzle-solving as a highlight. It may not be a graphical powerhouse, but Tenebris Somnia still maintains a creepy atmosphere thanks to solid scares partly delivered by effective and well-made live-action cinematics. If you’re going to binge horror films, you may as well play one too. You can read my full review here.

Full disclosure: I have not played One Piece: Grand Gourmet. I was trying to finish up Castlevania: Belmont's Curse when a review game landed in my lap that I've had to give my full attention. That said, I have watched a lot of the One Piece anime, have a cat named Nami, and dog named Luffy.

I don't know if One Piece: Grand Gourmet is any good, but I like the premise and pixel graphics. One Piece is a very malleable franchise (which is why its live action adaptation is pretty good), so the idea of managing a restaurant as Sanji feels like it could be a very good fit. I plan on climbing aboard with all my hopes and dreams soon. And it is out now, which is good to know.

Similar to the entry above, I have not yet played Stupid Never Dies yet (there are too many video games!), but we like to use this weekly article to call out the new video games of the week. I am eager to check out Stupid Never Dies primarily because of its pop-punk soundtrack and 2000s aesthetic. I think it has the potential to be a fun, nostalgic throwback to my youth when I was learning Blink-182's "Dammit" on guitar and playing Devil May Cry.

The Blood of Dawnwalker has been out for just over seven weeks now, but I wouldn't blame you if you haven't finished it – or even started it – yet. A lot has come out! But if you need a reason to jump back in, this week's 1.1 update is a great excuse – the devs have added hundreds of bug fixes and other minor improvements, so it should run better than it ever did before. There's also an even easier difficulty mode if you want to cruise through without worrying about combat, and a new in-game potion that lets you respec all your skill points. I stalled out about halfway through (when I started playing Wolverine), but I'm planning to jump back in this weekend.

Oh, and you can pet dogs and cats now. Maybe I should have led with that.

Multiplayer physics mountain-climbing game Peak became one of the most viral co-op experiences of 2025 (I refuse to use the term friendslop), but only PC players have enjoyed its wacky shenanigans. That changed this week as Peak is now available on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Switch 2. Either alone or, preferably, alongside up to three friends, you’ll try to ascend procedurally generated, absurdly unrealistic mountains riddled with dangers. Working together is key, a tricky prospect thanks to the in-game proximity chat that necessitates sticking together, but griefing each other, intentionally or otherwise, is just as entertaining – maddeningly frustrating at times, but entertaining. Peak on consoles includes all post-launch content and, best of all, supports crossplay for all platforms.

The original Azul remains one of my all-time favorite games even after many years, but it just misses the bar with its strategic complexity to be one I'd pull out to play with the kids. That why I was especially delighted to find that Azul Kids is one of those rare "adapted for children" projects that turned out extremely well.

Players take on the roll of creative young artists building mosaic displays with various colored tiles. The concept remains simple enough to work for even very young players of age five or six, but the whole family should have fun with the approachable strategy implications of choosing tiles and completing your masterpiece.

#4300. Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

Vince Zampella, co-creator of Call of Duty, and a veteran studio head responsible for some of the biggest franchises in the world, is gone.

Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

Zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”

Then you have the two best sorcerers, Gujo and Tuji, evolving to new heights. Tuji gets a damage buff and a brand new passive while Gujo - after his Infinity evolution - gets a damage boost, a freeze passive, and an SPA deduction.

Similarly, the other evolved versions - Tengon (Flashiness), Igros (Elite Knight), Vogito Super (Awakened), and Alocard (Vampire Knight) - also gain certain boosts and passives that make them worthy of the SS tier. Even after getting nerfed, they remain strong enough to destroy wave after wave of enemy units single-handedly.

Similarly, Julias (Eisplosion) gets massive damage and RNG. Moreover, every attack freezes the enemies, a handy little passive in every game mode.

Both the base and evolved versions of Obita end up in the same tier because the stats and performance remain pretty much the same. Obita (Awakened) looks a lot cooler, though.

The B-tier of our Anime Vanguards tier list has the highest population because average units are aplenty.

Some Epic units like Alligator, Blossom, and Kinnua have also ended up in our B tier, and that’s because they are the best ones out of the lot. On the other hand, we also have some Legendary units like Itochi, Kinaru, Vogita Super, and the brand-new Nobaba that fail to meet expectations.

The worst mythical character in the game, in my opinion, Sasuke (Hebi) is also a B-tier resident along with Noruto (Six Tales) and Obita. No, I don’t hate Naruto characters - maybe Starburst does.

#4298. Karmine Corp knock LCP’s last team out of Worlds 2026 to force a Swiss decider

Karmine Corp swept CTBC Flying Oyster 2-0 at Worlds 2026, eliminating the LCP's last remaining team. The French-based side move to 2-2 in the Swiss Stage, leaving one best-of-three between them and the quarter-finals.

The Round 4 tie began at 20:05 on Thursday 29 October and needed only two games. KC took the first game in 28 minutes and closed out the second in 37.

The result ends a run of two straight defeats. An opening victory over Anyone’s Legend had been followed by single-game losses in Rounds 2 and 3. They now have three games won and two lost in the event.

CFO were the higher seed, so they had first choice for game one. They took first pick, which put KC on the blue side. The opener was one-sided, with KC finishing on 18 kills to CFO’s three, according to GosuGamers.

Riot Games uses a five-round Swiss format. A team that reaches three match losses is knocked out. For CFO, this was a third defeat. Their opening win over Team Liquid was followed by losses to Movistar KOI and T1.

Before Worlds, CFO’s last two results came in LCP Split 3 2026: a 3-1 win over MVK Esports and a 0-3 defeat to Team Secret Whales.

The Elo power rankings show a wide gap between the sides. KC are 10th on a rating of 1796. CFO are 54th on 1638. The teams had met before, at the First Stand 2025 knockout stage on 15 March 2025, when KC won 3-2.

KC reached the Swiss Stage through the Play-In. They opened it on 15 October 2026 by edging Cloud9 in a five-game series. They then beat MVK Esports 3-0 in both the Upper Bracket Final and the Grand Final. Their roster is Canna, Yike, Busio, Caliste and Kyeahoo.

A team goes through to the Knockout Stage once it reaches three match wins. One more victory would send KC through, while one more defeat would end their campaign. The Knockout Stage is split between Allen and Brooklyn, New York. Quarter-finals run from 3 to 6 November and start at 10.00pm UTC.

#4297. Phantom Blade Zero Review In Progress – Shaping Up To Be One Of The Best Action Games I've Ever Played

Phantom Blade Zero is an astounding achievement for the action genre. So astounding that I feel pulled to experience everything it has to offer… and that means instead of rolling credits, I’ve been busy completing story-critical side quests and more to get the most complete ending. That’s another way of saying I am enjoying this game very, very much but still need more time to render a final verdict, which is why you’re reading a review-in-progress of Phantom Blade Zero rather than a scored piece.

Though I’m not interested in guesstimating a score right now, I know it will be high because Phantom Blade Zero impresses and then some. It is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and I’m shocked to be writing that. This is a debut of sorts for developer S-Game, which has dabbled in mobile games and smaller-scale titles; it’s the team’s first triple-A release, and its first game of this kind. This studio is so clearly a dedicated student of the genre, analyzing what works here and what works there in other action greats to create something of its own. It looks forward at what action games can do, can play like, can look like, while looking back at the games before it and understanding why those games – games like Devil May Cry, Elden Ring, Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, Bayonetta, and just about every other quality action game you can think of – continue to be ones we hold so highly. Should it stick the landing, Phantom Blade Zero will join that echelon of action pedigree.

Protagonist Soul is a quiet, mostly stoic martial arts master who prefers to let his blades (of which there are so, so many) do the talking. The Order he’s sworn his life to betrays him, and, in an effort to right wrongs, he discovers a villainous conspiracy to seize full power of the blood-soaked Chinese martial underground known as Wulin. As a result, puppets, secret sects, powerful god-like creatures, monstrous beasts, and much more prowl Wulin’s various biomes. I haven’t kept count, but there are a massive number of enemies to take down, both standard mob variants and bosses, and the game stays fresh throughout. It's even fresher when you consider how many weapons you can acquire on Soul’s journey.

Every weapon is wholly unique, like picking up a new character in a fighting game, each with its own moveset and abilities. Upgrading these weapons through various tiers unlocks additional abilities, and you can even Soul Temper weapons to add one final, game-changing ability or perk. A fully upgraded weapon can have a moveset that uses the majority of buttons on your controller. You can do the same with Phantom Edges, special tide-turning weapons with limited uses (before you build up additional charges). Combined with different accessories and medicine types, Phantom Blade Zero offers hundreds, perhaps thousands, of combat kit permutations. You can play as a drunken fighter who switches between sober, tipsy, and drunken states, with his range and damage output changing as a result; you can focus on a bleed build, ripping enemies to shreds with charged attacks that utilize Soul's own HP to deal extra damage (that can then be earned back with bleed); you can use lightning, wind, fire, and ice to create elemental storms against enemies, and you can use a sword that switches between different elemental states on command as well. You can also just pound enemies to pulp with Phantom Edge fists, too. I’ve struggled to stop using these fists since acquiring them because they’re so satisfying.

Forty-plus hours into Phantom Blade Zero, it feels like I’ve played as dozens of different Souls because I've discovered so many build types. S-Game smartly pushes you to try new builds and weapons as you get them, doling out generous upgrade materials and currency; it encourages you to try everything, and the next weapon might just become your new favorite.

Finding these materials (and additional fights) is great fun, too, because Phantom Blade Zero’s various open-area biomes are a genuine joy to explore. You are always rewarded for taking the optional path, and those rewards are always worthwhile. You might find a healthy pile of upgrade materials, or a boss with a weapon you’ll fall in love with. The way buildings, alleys, caves, cliffsides, and other environmental features weave in and out of each other evokes FromSoftware’s architectural design and the subsequent shortcut “aha!” moments.

That said, Phantom Blade Zero is definitively not a Soulslike, though you’d be forgiven for assuming as much given its challenging suite of bosses, interconnected world, and Phantom Bell checkpoints, which are this game’s equivalent of bonfires. However, its challenge is much more surmountable (with various difficulties and accessories to ease parry and dodge timing), and its world progression is materially different. Kill an enemy and it’s dead for good, which to my surprise, adds a sense of worldbuilding I didn’t know I wanted. Progression through this journey feels tangible because I’m actually removing traces of evil with my weapons, traces that don’t respawn when I interact with checkpoints. It’s a nice change of pace that narratively speaks to Soul’s efforts.

Along the way, countless reading materials shed light on Phantom Blade Zero’s intertwining stories, and tracking down the next memory, scroll, or book entry rewards you if you’re interested in the full picture of this Wuxia story. I’d argue the game’s story is its weakest element, but only when compared to the rest of the package. It doesn't break any new ground narratively, but it provides enough mystery and thrill to keep things moving. And while performances are great, talking to characters is still mostly just two people standing across from each other talking through a new quest. Fortunately, cutscenes pick up the slack with dramatic villains, heartfelt revelations, raw tension, and more.

Production value is high across the board, thanks to incredibly impressive animation and a beautiful rendering of this dark fantasy China. Faces are lifelike, nudging up just shy of the uncanny valley as close-ups reveal porous details, lip quivers, and more, bringing an excellent cast of Chinese performances to life. The English voice acting has its standouts, but Soul’s voice is boring, so I highly recommend the Chinese vocals.

Boss fights draw clear inspiration from Chinese cinema and boast a wondrous sense of awe and scale that only the best in the genre typically offer. There are a ton of bosses, too, with very few repeats (repeats do happen in segmented challenge trials), and it’s impressive to think back on just how many I defeated, and just how many of them delivered a unique fight. I appreciate the checkpoints between boss phases as well. There are so many bosses – nearing 100 or more if I had to guess – and having my progression saved through phases removes some of the repetition I often feel when, say, phase two of a boss continues to kill me and I have to blitz through phase one again and again before taking another stab at it.

That scale and on-screen excitement carry through almost every fight in the game, down to even the simplest mob fights, though these are starting to feel a touch repetitive as I’m barreling toward the game’s end. Soul moves like the world’s greatest martial artist, but your controller inputs make it happen. If you mash the attack button, it looks nice… but if you use each weapon’s prescribed inputs and abilities, Phantom Blade Zero delivers a level of detailed action I’ve seen in few other games. You direct the game’s action, and this lets you turn what might otherwise be just another group of fodder enemies into an electric bout of spectacle.

To say I greatly enjoy this game greatly undersells my feelings – writing this review-in-progress is frustrating because I want to get back to Phantom Blade Zero. I expect to reach credits in the coming days, so please be on the lookout for my final verdict this week.

If you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros update brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

#4295. Aonuma Calls the Water Temple His 'Overdue Homework' for Ocarina of Time Remake

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

With the release of the full remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo Switch 2 later this week, old-school fans have been once again reminiscing on their many fond and not-so-fond memories from the N64 original. Whenever the topic of Ocarina of Time comes up, it’s often a safe bet that, sooner or later, things will turn to the infamous Water Temple, one of the elemental-themed dungeons in the game’s back half.

The Water Temple has long held a reputation for being one of the most legendarily frustrating dungeons in the Zelda franchise. Admittedly, a lot of the discourse is hyperbolic, based on memories of collective childhood, but the dungeon also definitely had some irritating quirks, from its confusing layout to the way it forced you to use your items and menus. If you didn’t have the little jingle that played every time you opened the pause menu permanently seared into your head before that dungeon, you sure did afterward.

The first gameplay trailer for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has confirmed that it has added a beloved feature from the 3DS version.

The designers of the Ocarina of Time remake are very aware of the long-standing vibe toward the Water Temple, as they discussed in an Ask the Developer feature on Nintendo’s official blog. Eiji Aonuma, the director and dungeon designer of the original game, now a senior officer and producer on the remake, spoke on how he created the original dungeon and how his perspective has changed since, with the remake’s director, Hokwai Ng, discussing how they’re making improvements without changing the fundamental vibe of the dungeon.

As part of the interview, Aonuma, Ng, and other members of the development team were asked how they approached the development of dungeons in the Ocarina of Time remake, particularly in relation to the original.

With a laugh, Aonuma said, “I had some overdue homework: I wanted to do something about the Water Temple I created 28 years ago.” He said that, back in the days of the N64, there were very few games that allowed you to do much of anything in an underwater setting. Therefore, if he was going to make an underwater dungeon, he wanted it to be distinct, something that brings across what could make being in such an environment fun. Aonuma is actually a hobbyist freediver, so he’s very acquainted with the distinct sensations of being completely underwater.

If he was going to make an underwater dungeon, he wanted it to be distinct, something that brings across what could make being in such an environment fun.

However, he concedes that the biggest problem with the Water Temple was one of navigation. “With the dungeon’s complex structure and a lot of item toggling involved, you often had to open the menu screen repeatedly, making it hard to keep track of where you were and which way you were facing.”

A look at the Water Temple from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and how it should be remade with the same design.

Aonuma explained that, given the infamy that the Water Temple has accrued due to its difficulty, he had the dev team make some adjustments, not necessarily to make it flat-out easier, but to make it more playable and user-friendly.

Ng chimed in here to explain the team’s perspective, noting that most of the dungeon’s basic mechanisms have been preserved, but the layout has been slightly shifted in places to improve the overall signposting and flow of the dungeon. Additionally, some of the walls of the temple have been changed to a distinct lattice pattern, allowing you to see bits of the temple beyond the current room and get a better idea of where you are in relation to everything else, which will hopefully keep players from getting lost. Finally, item toggling has been streamlined, so you don’t need to keep opening the menu to equip and unequip your Iron Boots.

Are you excited for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake? So are we! Here are 8 changes we would like to see implemented in the remake.

At the end of the interview, Ng added that he hopes the slight differences between the remake and the original will spark some inter-generational conversation. He imagined a father playing the game with his child and saying, “You know, your Dad got stuck in the Water Temple plenty of times back in the day.”

Aonuma laughed and responded, “Then kids playing this version might say, “Come on, it’s not that hard.” Poor old Dad might end up feeling deflated.”

#4293. Report: Ghost Of Yōtei Developer Sucker Punch Hit With Layoffs

Sucker Punch, the team behind Ghost of Yōtei, Ghost of Tsushima, Infamous, and Sly Cooper, has been hit with layoffs, according to a report by Aftermath. The outlet states that 26 roles have been affected as the studio prepares its next project.

Aftermath cites a former Sucker Punch employee who confirmed the number of layoffs. The outlet also obtained a company email announcing the staff cuts.

“After carefully observing the challenges in the market and reviewing the team needs for our next project, we've decided to make some staffing reductions. Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

Gentle Mates GC, on their Championship debut, beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 2-1 in the upper bracket final in São Paulo. The French-based side go into Sunday's best-of-five grand final with a two-map ban advantage, while Shopify Rebellion Gold must come through the lower final.

Gentle Mates GC are into the grand final of the VCT Game Changers Championship 2026. They beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 2-1 in the upper bracket final in São Paulo on Friday 30 October. The French-based side dropped the opening map and then took the next two. Both teams had arrived at the match with every map at the event won.

Shopify Rebellion Gold won map one, which lasted 53 minutes. On the second map they fought back to 10-10, but Gentle Mates closed it out 13-11 after 55 minutes. The decider on Summit ran for 57 minutes and finished 13-10 to Gentle Mates.

Coming through the upper bracket gives Gentle Mates a two-map ban advantage in the grand final. Shopify Rebellion Gold, led at the event by interim in-game leader alexis, drop into the lower bracket final against KRÜ Blaze.

This is Gentle Mates’ first appearance at the Championship. Their line-up of Marti, Nami, Wens, tokameite and berryx reached the upper final with 2-0 wins over Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC. Their last three EMEA Stage 3 results before the event were wins over G2 Gozen and SK Nebula, both 2-1, and a 3-2 defeat to G2 Gozen.

The Elo power rankings already had Gentle Mates ahead. They sit fourth with a rating of 1844 and a 33-7 record from 40 rated matches. Shopify Rebellion Gold are sixth on 1809, with a 40-20 record from 60 rated matches.

Shopify Rebellion Gold had cleared SK Nebula and KRÜ Blaze without losing a map. Before travelling, they beat FlyQuest RED 3-1 and 2-1 and SwimTrek Blue 2-0 in North America Stage 2. At last year’s Championship in Seoul, Team Liquid Brazil beat them 3-2 in the title match.

The lower bracket final is a rematch. Shopify Rebellion Gold beat KRÜ Blaze in the upper semi-final. KRÜ then earned their place with lower bracket wins over Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC, both without dropping a map. MIBR GC finished fourth, which is worth $50,000. SK Nebula, one of three EMEA teams in São Paulo, placed joint fifth to sixth for $25,000. Their line-up included Scottish player fluxxy.

ON VA EN FINALE DES WORLDS ! pic.twitter.com/vAt2vVdyvY

— Gentle Mates (@gentlemates) October 30, 2026

Third place pays $70,000. The lower bracket final and the grand final are both best-of-five, after best-of-three series in the earlier rounds of the double-elimination bracket. Ten teams entered the event at Riot Games Arena, which Riot describes as the last Game Changers Championship to be held as a standalone event. In 2027 the Championship moves to Austin, Texas. For the first time it will run in the same city at the same time as VALORANT Champions, from 16 September to 10 October.

Shopify Rebellion Gold and KRÜ Blaze meet in the lower bracket final on Saturday 31 October at 15:00 BRT. The winner faces Gentle Mates GC in the grand final on Sunday 1 November at 15:00 BRT.

#4290. DC Worlds Collide tier list - The famous debate of which superheroes are the most powerful

How powerful is every character in DC Worlds Collide? Today, we will break them all down, one by one, and present you with a complete DC Worlds Collide tier list.

After being closed for a while (since 2022), DC Worlds Collide re-launched, and although it still retains some of its older features, it is now kinda updated, and a lot more user-friendly. The best Legendary & Epic characters in DC Worlds Collide Epic is the highest hero rarity you can get from the normal gacha banner, called the Epic Recruitment. Of course, there are also Legendary heroes, which are a step above the Epics. However, not all the Legendaries are created equal - Wonder Woman is one of the absolute best picks, hands-down.

In this DC Worlds Collide tier list, we've not ranked the Elite and below characters, since you won't be using them past the starter stages. Instead, if any of them are worthy of being ranked, you will find them in the tier list; otherwise, they're not good end-game characters.

DC Worlds Collide tier list Since we ranked all the rarest characters (Epic and Legendary), we sorted them from the S+ tier, which is the highest, all the way down to the C tier, which is the lowest.
